title: You’ll trust God to split an ocean…
paragraphs:
You’ll trust God to split an ocean…
but lose sleep over a notification.
Let that sit.

Because this isn’t about your situation.
It’s about your trust.

We sing about miracles.
We post about breakthroughs.
We shout “God is able!”

But when the problem is small—
suddenly, your chest tightens…
your mind races…
your faith goes silent.
Why?

Because big problems force surrender.
Small problems expose control.

When the diagnosis comes, you pray.
When the relationship breaks, you cry out.
When everything collapses, you kneel.
But when it’s just:

A delayed reply…
A tight budget…
A stressful week…
You don’t surrender.
You strategize.

You grip harder.
You think faster.
You carry it yourself.
And you call that wisdom.
But Scripture cuts deeper than that.
“Whoever is faithful in very little is also faithful in much…” — Luke 16:10
Read that again.

Faith isn’t proven in the spotlight of miracles.
It’s revealed in the shadows of ordinary life.
Let me say something uncomfortable:
You don’t struggle to trust God because your problems are big.
You struggle to trust God because your heart still wants to be God.
Look at Peter.

He stepped out of the boat.
He believed the impossible.

But the moment the wind felt real—
he sank.

Same water.
Same Jesus.
Different focus.
That’s us.

We trust God in theory…
but doubt Him in reality.

We declare His power…
but question His care.

We believe He can raise the dead—
but wonder if He notices our daily stress.
Here’s the truth:

If God is only God in your big moments…
then He’s not truly God in your life.

Because the same God who parts seas
also counts hairs on your head (Matthew 10:30).

The same God who raises the dead
also feeds birds you never notice (Matthew 6:26).
Nothing is “small” to a God who is infinite.
The issue isn’t His ability.
It’s our attention.
And this is where the Gospel confronts us.

Not gently.
But truthfully.
Your inconsistency in trusting God isn’t just weakness.
It’s sin.

Because every moment you choose anxiety over trust—
you are saying:
“God, I don’t believe You’re enough for this.”
That’s heavy.
But don’t run from it.
Because grace meets you right there.
Jesus didn’t just die for your worst day.
He died for your daily unbelief.

Every silent doubt.
Every hidden worry.
Every moment you chose control over surrender—
He carried it to the cross.
Fully.
Completely.
Paid.

And when Jesus Christ rose again,
He didn’t just secure your eternity.
He secured your today.

Your Monday anxiety.
Your financial pressure.
Your unanswered prayers.
He didn’t rise so you could trust Him only in crises.
He rose so you could trust Him in everything.
So what do we do now?
Not perform.
Not pretend.
Not try to manufacture stronger faith.
We return.
Return with the small things.

That message you’re overthinking?
Give it to Him.

That bill stressing you out?
Bring it to Him.

That quiet fear you haven’t told anyone?
Lay it down.
Because real faith isn’t loud.
It’s consistent.
It whispers:
“God, even here… I trust You.”

And maybe—just maybe—
the greatest miracle in your life won’t be a parted sea.
It will be this:

A heart that finally rests
in the middle of ordinary chaos.
Listen…

God is not waiting for a bigger problem
so He can prove Himself to you.

He’s waiting for you
to trust Him in what you already have.
So today, don’t just worship Him for what He can do.

Trust Him for what He’s already doing—
even in the unnoticed, uncelebrated, ordinary spaces of your life.
Pause.
Pray.
Surrender one “small” thing right now.
And comment one word:
Let heaven witness your decision.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
